title: Three Startups Reinventing Critical Infrastructure

reader_summary.headline: Three startups reinvent ocean, mining, and nuclear power infrastructure.
reader_summary.overview: The episode explains how new companies are fixing broken systems in the ocean, mining, and energy. They use robots, AI, and portable reactors to solve problems that big industries ignored. These startups aim to make critical infrastructure safer, faster, and more efficient.

key_points.text: Ulysses builds cheap, autonomous robots that work together to solve tough problems in the ocean.

key_points.text: China is building advanced underwater drones that can reach US coastlines, creating a serious security threat.

thesis: The episode highlights three A16Z portfolio companies—Ulysses, Mariana Minerals, and Radiant—that are reinventing critical infrastructure through underwater robotics, modern mineral extraction technologies, and nuclear microreactors, respectively. Ulysses specifically argues that the ocean remains an underexplored frontier due to a historical narrative shift and classification that left the sector reliant on outdated tools, positioning their autonomous vehicle platform as the necessary 'SpaceX for the ocean' to solve critical tasks in conservation, commercial energy, and defense.
